note: All puzzles were picked from the full bank (not retired) and their answers were checked visually against the figures. Do not change answers. Option images are option_<LETTER>.png; angle ranking and cube counting have text options.

puzzles.question: Which opening could the object pass through?
puzzles.rule_line: The object can't rotate once it starts through. Only one opening fits.
puzzles.why_it_fits: D is the object's exact outline seen straight on: the bottom gap and the V-notch match in size and position.

traps.A: The outline of a different side, changed so it can't pass.
traps.B: Looks almost like D, but it adds a feature the object doesn't show from that side. Compare carefully, not just the overall shape.
traps.C: A different side's outline, changed so it can't pass.
traps.E: A different side's outline, changed so it can't pass.

puzzles.question: Which drawing is the missing FRONT view?
puzzles.rule_line: Solid lines = visible edges. Dashed lines = hidden edges.
puzzles.why_it_fits: The two cut corners in the top view face you, so both show up as solid lines near each end of the front view.

traps.A: Right kind of line, but only one end shows it. A corner is missing.
traps.B: One edge is drawn dashed, but it faces you, so it must be solid.
traps.C: A visible edge is drawn dashed. Solid and hidden lines are swapped.

puzzles.question: Rank the four angles from SMALLEST to LARGEST.
puzzles.rule_line: Ignore line length. Only the opening between the lines counts.
puzzles.why_it_fits: 4 is narrowest (about 38 deg), then 3 (about 42 deg), then 1 (about 47 deg), and 2 is widest (about 52 deg).

traps.B: Swaps 3 and 4, the two closest angles. Long arms on 4 make it look bigger.
traps.C: Swaps 1 and 2, the two widest angles.
traps.D: The right idea, but ranked largest to smallest. Read the question twice.

puzzles.question: The paper is folded, then punched through all layers. Which is the unfolded pattern?
puzzles.rule_line: Unfold in reverse order. Every hole mirrors across each fold it went through.
puzzles.why_it_fits: The hole is punched in column 3. Undo fold 2 and it mirrors into column 2. Undo fold 1 and that mirrors into column 1. That's 3 holes across the top row.

traps.A: Only 1 hole. Both folds were ignored.
traps.C: 4 holes. Column 4 was never folded, so it gets no hole.
traps.D: A hole is shifted down one row.
traps.E: A hole is shifted by one cell.

puzzles.question: How many cubes have exactly 5 painted faces?
puzzles.rule_line: The whole figure is painted on every exposed side except the bottom.
puzzles.why_it_fits: Only the top cube of each tower has 5 painted faces: its top plus all 4 sides. Its bottom rests on the cube below. There are 3 towers, so 3 cubes.

traps.A: Counts 2 too few. Check every tower, including the short one on the left.
traps.D: Counts 1 too many. A cube with a neighbour beside it loses a painted side.

puzzles.question: Which cube does the pattern fold into?
puzzles.rule_line: Track where the dark face and the dark band end up, and which way the band runs.
puzzles.why_it_fits: A puts the solid dark face and the half-dark band on the right faces, with the band running the right way.

traps.B: The band is on the right face but turned the wrong way.
traps.C: The band is on the right face but turned the wrong way.
traps.D: The shading is on the wrong face.

puzzles.question: SUNDAY CHALLENGE: Which solid does the pattern fold into?
puzzles.rule_line: All four look alike. Compare proportions, not just shape.
puzzles.why_it_fits: C is the only option whose proportions match the pattern's faces.

traps.A: The right kind of solid, but its proportions are off.
traps.B: The right kind of solid, but its proportions are off.
traps.D: This pattern can't fold into it: a face has the wrong shape.
